record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: Extend and generalize to planar rational systems the boundedness and convergence trichotomy known for x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g x_{n-1})/(A + B x_n + C x_{n-1}), with nonnegative parameters and positive denominators: if C > 0 then every solution is bounded; if C = 0 and B > 0, every solution is bounded exactly when g <= b + A; when g = b + A every solution converges to a not necessarily prime period-two solution; and when g < b + A every solution has a finite limit. The problem is to find the corresponding planar-system generalization, including the right hypotheses and alternatives.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the scalar third-order-type rational difference equation
  x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g x_{n-1}) / (A + B x_n + C x_{n-1}),  n = 0, 1, 2, …,
with nonnegative parameters a, b, g, A, B, C and nonnegative initial conditions x_{-1}, x_0 chosen so that the denominator is positive for all n. For this equation the following trichotomy is known:
 (i) If C > 0, then every solution is bounded.
 (ii) If C = 0 and B > 0, then every solution is bounded if and only if g ≤ b + A; moreover,
   – when g = b + A every solution converges to a (not necessarily prime) period-two solution, and
   – when g < b + A every solution has a finite limit.

Now consider a planar system of rational difference equations of the form
  x_{n+1} = (α_1 + β_1 x_n + γ_1 y_n) / (A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n),
  y_{n+1} = (α_2 + β_2 x_n + γ_2 y_n) / (A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n),
with nonnegative coefficients and nonnegative initial data such that both denominators remain positive for every n ≥ 0 (and more generally any planar rational system that arises as a natural two-dimensional analogue of the scalar equation above).

Formulate and prove the planar-system analogue of the trichotomy: identify the precise hypotheses on the coefficients of the planar system under which every solution is bounded, the precise sharp conditions separating the bounded from the unbounded regime, and the corresponding global dynamical alternatives (convergence to an equilibrium versus convergence to a period-two solution) that replace cases (i) and (ii).
artifact.status_search_result: Research on rational systems in the plane (Camouzis, Ladas, Garić-Demirović, Palladino, and others) has settled the global behavior for several specific families of planar rational systems, but no source found gives a complete planar-system trichotomy fully generalizing the scalar (a+bx+gx_{n-1})/(A+Bx_n+Cx_{n-1}) result with sharp boundedness/convergence alternatives. The general problem appears to remain open, with only partial results for special subclasses.
